name: What is the difference between an ADU and a JADU?

mainEntity.name: What is the difference between an ADU and a JADU?

acceptedAnswer.text: An ADU (Accessory Dwelling Unit) is an independent living unit that can be attached, detached, or a converted space. A JADU (Junior Accessory Dwelling Unit) is a smaller, more restricted unit, always located within the existing walls of a single-family home, including an attached garage. JADUs are generally limited to 500 square feet and may share a bathroom or have efficiency kitchens, unlike full ADUs.
acceptedAnswer.description: An ADU is a full independent living unit, while a JADU is a smaller unit (under 500 sq ft) located within an existing home, potentially sharing facilities.
